slices.focus: Comprehensive onboarding — personal, family, work, finances, health, and life goals
slices.summary: Derek introduces himself comprehensively: a 41-year-old journeyman wireman for IBEW Local 5 in Pittsburgh, recently pulled into part-time apprenticeship instruction and safety coordination. He details his family (wife Erin, two kids, brother Logan), ongoing housing renovation, chronic back issues, and his life goal of building a retention-focused apprenticeship training system that raises first-to-third-year retention above 80 percent. The conversation establishes his ISTJ personality, dry humor under pressure, and preference for straightforward practical communication.

Derek documents the near-miss formally, which escalates to a tense training center debrief where veteran staff react defensively. He is informally tasked with reviewing first-year ladder and lockout-tagout instruction, representing a significant though unofficial role shift toward programmatic safety leadership. The incident sharpens his focus but also worsens his sleep as he replays the avoidable nature of the event.

slices.focus: Labor history podcast discovery through Mike's garage day shifts commute habits
slices.summary: Derek spends a Sunday at Mike Cercone's garage sorting pipe fittings and listening to a Mon Valley labor history podcast. The combination of hands-on work and compelling local history unexpectedly helps quiet his anxious mental loops. This experience leads him to replace default sports radio with labor and trade history podcasts on his early morning drives, a small but meaningful shift that Erin notices and appreciates.

Ron Belski pushes back hard, calling the check-ins 'hand-holding,' but the evidence is strong enough that the pilot launches despite resistance. Derek wrestles with how to protect the core while letting the old guard save face.
